12  Simulating from saved fits

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code

Generate and save responses for a named collection of fitted models. Reconstruct each model from its fit record, preserve the observation and participant assignments, and optionally inspect configured behavioral summaries. This procedure performs no optimization.

12.1 Parameters and setup

fit_paths names the saved results. A one-entry mapping runs one model. trial_query=None uses the exact recorded rows; an explicit query specifies a new simulation selection. Saved records supply the factories, components, fixed settings and feature paths. Use distinct output folders for independent work units.

Each fit_paths entry may also name a directory of participant-fit JSON files from separate jobs. The notebook combines matching specifications, orders parameter rows by participant ID and retains each participant’s recorded observations. Duplicate IDs and incompatible specifications are rejected. A directory produces <entry name>.h5; individual files retain their recorded output names. Upload custom fit directories yourself when running in Colab. Older fit files may omit the simulator: specify sim_alg_path in that case. A supplied value overrides the recorded simulator.

1 — Configure the saved fits and simulation work unit 
# Observations and work-unit selection
data_path = "data/Dupertuys2026.h5"

# Saved model fits
fit_paths = {
    "CMR": "data/fits/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo.json",
    "eCMR_source_only": "data/fits/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_source_only.json",
    "eCMR_broad": "data/fits/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_broad.json",
}
model_labels = {
    "CMR": "CMR",
    "eCMR_source_only": "Source-only eCMR",
    "eCMR_broad": "Broader eCMR",
}

# Output locations and regeneration

simulation_dir = "results/simulations"
trial_query = None
max_subjects = 0

# Simulation settings

simulation_seed = 1

3 — Import packages 
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

import jaxcmr
from jaxcmr import repetition
from jaxcmr.helpers import (
    generate_trial_mask,
    import_from_string,
    load_data,
    save_dict_to_hdf5,
    save_figure,
)

4 — Define feature loading and model construction 
def load_features(spec):
    semantic = np.load(spec["embedding_path"]) if spec.get("embedding_path") else None
    categorical = (
        np.load(spec["emotion_feature_path"])[
            :,
            int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) : int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) + 1,
        ]
        if spec.get("emotion_feature_path")
        else None
    )
    if (
        spec.get("concat_features", False)
        and categorical is not None
        and semantic is not None
    ):
        return np.concatenate([categorical, semantic], axis=1)
    return categorical if categorical is not None else semantic


def construct_model(spec):
    return import_from_string(spec["model_factory"])(
        **{name: import_from_string(path) for name, path in spec["components"].items()}
    )

data_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(data_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()

6 — Define participant-fit compatibility checks 
def check_participant_fit(
    participant_record,
    reference_record,
    previous_subjects,
    specification_keys,
    model_name,
):
    """Reject incompatible specifications, duplicate IDs and misaligned columns."""
    if any(
        participant_record.get(key) != reference_record.get(key)
        for key in specification_keys
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{model_name}: participant fits have incompatible model or input specifications."
        )
    participant_ids = participant_record["fits"]["subject"]
    if participant_record.get("pooled", False) or -1 in participant_ids:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{model_name}: directories must contain participant fits, not pooled fits."
        )
    if len(set(participant_ids)) != len(participant_ids) or set(participant_ids) & set(
        previous_subjects
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"{model_name}: duplicate participant IDs in fit directory.")
    if set(participant_record["fits"]) != set(reference_record["fits"]) or any(
        len(v) != len(participant_ids) for v in participant_record["fits"].values()
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{model_name}: fit columns must match and contain one value per participant."
        )
7 — Define participant-file combination 
def combine_participant_fits(participant_records, data, model_name):
    """Combine compatible participant estimates without losing their identities."""
    subjects = np.asarray(data["subject"]).ravel()
    specification_keys = (
        "model_factory",
        "components",
        "simulation_function",
        "loss_function",
        "data_sha256",
        "fixed",
        "free",
        "embedding_path",
        "emotion_feature_path",
        "feature_column",
        "concat_features",
    )
    reference_record = participant_records[0]
    combined_parameters = {key: [] for key in reference_record["fits"]}
    selected_rows = set()
    for participant_record in participant_records:
        check_participant_fit(
            participant_record,
            reference_record,
            combined_parameters["subject"],
            specification_keys,
            model_name,
        )
        participant_ids = participant_record["fits"]["subject"]
        for key in combined_parameters:
            combined_parameters[key].extend(participant_record["fits"][key])
        if "selected_trial_indices" in participant_record:
            rows = participant_record["selected_trial_indices"]
            if not np.isin(subjects[rows], participant_ids).all():
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{model_name}: recorded observation rows belong to another participant."
                )
        else:
            mask = generate_trial_mask(
                data,
                participant_record.get(
                    "trial_query", participant_record.get("data_query")
                ),
            )
            rows = np.flatnonzero(
                np.asarray(mask) & np.isin(subjects, participant_ids)
            ).tolist()
        selected_rows.update(rows)
    order = np.argsort(combined_parameters["subject"])
    combined_record = {
        key: reference_record[key]
        for key in specification_keys
        if key in reference_record
    }
    combined_record.update(
        name=model_name,
        label=reference_record.get("label", model_name),
        pooled=False,
        fits={
            key: np.asarray(values)[order].tolist()
            for key, values in combined_parameters.items()
        },
        selected_trial_indices=sorted(selected_rows),
    )
    # Preserve boolean settings as recorded before the fitter's numeric conversion.
    combined_record["fixed"] = (
        reference_record.get("fit_configuration", {})
        .get("parameters", {})
        .get("fixed", reference_record["fixed"])
    )
    return combined_record
8 — Define simulation-cache comparison 
def simulation_matches(saved_metadata, expected_configuration):
    """Compare the scientific settings, accepting the older provenance layout."""
    saved_metadata = dict(saved_metadata)
    implementation = saved_metadata.get("implementation", {})
    for key in ("jaxcmr_version", "jax_enable_x64"):
        saved_metadata.setdefault(key, implementation.get(key))
    return all(
        saved_metadata.get(key) == value
        for key, value in expected_configuration.items()
    )

12.2 Reconstruct the saved specifications

9 — Read named fit files or participant-fit directories 
fit_paths = {model_name: Path(path) for model_name, path in fit_paths.items()}
records = {}
for model_name, path in fit_paths.items():
    if not path.is_dir():
        records[model_name] = json.loads(path.read_text())
        continue
    participant_records = [
        json.loads(file.read_text()) for file in sorted(path.glob("*.json"))
    ]
    if not participant_records:
        raise ValueError(f"{model_name}: no participant-fit JSON files in {path}.")
    if sim_alg_path is not None:
        for participant_record in participant_records:
            participant_record["simulation_function"] = sim_alg_path
    records[model_name] = combine_participant_fits(
        participant_records, data, model_name
    )
    print(
        model_name,
        "— combined",
        len(participant_records),
        "files for",
        len(records[model_name]["fits"]["subject"]),
        "participants",
    )
if not records:
    raise ValueError("Supply at least one saved fit.")
display_labels = {
    model_name: model_labels.get(model_name, record.get("label", model_name))
    for model_name, record in records.items()
}
10 — Select matching observations for each fit 
selections = {}
for name, record in records.items():
    if sim_alg_path is not None:
        record["simulation_function"] = sim_alg_path
    if "simulation_function" not in record:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{name}: supply sim_alg_path for a fit without a recorded simulator."
        )
    if record.get("data_sha256", data_sha256) != data_sha256:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: the fit refers to a different observation file.")
    if trial_query is None and "selected_trial_indices" in record:
        mask = (
            jnp.zeros(len(subjects), dtype=bool)
            .at[jnp.asarray(record["selected_trial_indices"], dtype=int)]
            .set(True)
        )
    else:
        mask = generate_trial_mask(
            data,
            trial_query
            if trial_query is not None
            else record.get("trial_query", record.get("data_query")),
        )
    subject_ids = np.unique(subjects)
    if max_subjects:
        subject_ids = subject_ids[:max_subjects]
    if subject_indices:
        subject_ids = subject_ids[np.asarray(subject_indices, dtype=int)]
    mask &= jnp.isin(data["subject"].ravel(), subject_ids)
    if not record.get("pooled", record["fits"]["subject"] == [-1]):
        mask &= jnp.isin(
            data["subject"].ravel(), jnp.asarray(record["fits"]["subject"])
        )
    if not bool(mask.any()):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: no observations match the selected work unit.")
    selections[name] = mask
    print(display_labels[name], "—", int(mask.sum()), "lists; fit:", fit_paths[name])
comparison_mask = jnp.logical_or.reduce(jnp.stack(list(selections.values())), axis=0)

Source-only eCMR — 492 lists; fit: data/fits/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_source_only.json
Broader eCMR — 492 lists; fit: data/fits/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_broad.json
11 — Prepare response and figure paths 
simulation_dir = Path(simulation_dir) if simulation_dir is not None else output_dir
figure_dir = Path(figure_dir) if figure_dir is not None else output_dir
figure_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
simulation_paths = {
    name: simulation_dir / f"{record['name']}.h5" for name, record in records.items()
}
if len(set(simulation_paths.values())) != len(simulation_paths):
    raise ValueError("Fit records need distinct names for saved response files.")

12.3 Save simulated responses

Each response file has a sidecar recording the actual fitted parameters, observation rows, model and simulator, random seed, repetition count, package version and precision. Matching files may be reused when redo_sims=False. Pooled values are assigned to the original participant IDs. The default simulator forces observed recall counts; it does not predict stopping.

After editing the model implementation locally, set redo_sims=True to regenerate responses. Cache matching uses the recorded inputs and package version, not a scan of source files.

12 — Prepare participant parameters and response provenance 
simulation_inputs = {}
for model_name, fit_record in records.items():
    model_factory = construct_model(fit_record)
    features = load_features(fit_record)
    selected_trials = selections[model_name]
    is_pooled = fit_record.get("pooled", fit_record["fits"]["subject"] == [-1])
    participant_ids = jnp.unique(data["subject"].ravel()[selected_trials])
    subject_parameters = {
        key: jnp.asarray(values) for key, values in fit_record["fits"].items()
    }
    if is_pooled:
        subject_parameters = {
            key: jnp.repeat(values, len(participant_ids))
            for key, values in subject_parameters.items()
            if key != "subject"
        }
        subject_parameters["subject"] = participant_ids
    fixed = (
        fit_record.get("fit_configuration", {})
        .get("parameters", {})
        .get("fixed", fit_record["fixed"])
    )
    for key, value in fixed.items():
        if isinstance(value, bool):
            subject_parameters[key] = subject_parameters[key].astype(bool)
    configuration = {
        "fits": fit_record["fits"],
        "pooled": is_pooled,
        "jax_enable_x64": enable_x64,
        "jaxcmr_version": jaxcmr.__version__,
        "model_factory": fit_record["model_factory"],
        "components": fit_record["components"],
        "simulation_function": fit_record["simulation_function"],
        "data_sha256": data_sha256,
        "selected_trial_indices": np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(selected_trials)).tolist(),
        "feature_sha256": hashlib.sha256(features.tobytes()).hexdigest()
        if features is not None
        else None,
        "seed": simulation_seed,
        "experiment_count": experiment_count,
    }
    simulation_inputs[model_name] = {
        "model_factory": model_factory,
        "features": features,
        "parameters": subject_parameters,
        "trial_mask": selected_trials,
        "configuration": configuration,
    }
13 — Generate or reuse matching responses and save them 
simulations = {}
for model_name, prepared in simulation_inputs.items():
    model_factory = prepared["model_factory"]
    features = prepared["features"]
    subject_parameters = prepared["parameters"]
    selected_trials = prepared["trial_mask"]
    configuration = prepared["configuration"]
    simulation_path = simulation_paths[model_name]
    metadata_path = simulation_path.with_suffix(".json")
    saved_metadata = (
        json.loads(metadata_path.read_text()) if metadata_path.exists() else {}
    )
    reuse_responses = (
        not redo_sims
        and simulation_path.exists()
        and metadata_path.exists()
        and simulation_matches(saved_metadata, configuration)
    )
    if reuse_responses:
        simulated = load_data(str(simulation_path))
        print("Loaded matching responses:", simulation_path)
    else:
        simulated = simulate_h5_from_h5(
            model_factory,
            data,
            features,
            subject_parameters,
            selected_trials,
            experiment_count=experiment_count,
            rng=jax.random.PRNGKey(simulation_seed),
            simulate_trial_fn=import_from_string(configuration["simulation_function"]),
        )
        simulation_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        save_dict_to_hdf5(simulated, str(simulation_path))
        metadata_path.write_text(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    **configuration,
                    "jaxcmr_version": jaxcmr.__version__,
                    "jax_version": jax.__version__,
                },
                indent=2,
            )
            + "\n"
        )
        print("Saved responses:", simulation_path)
    if filter_repeated_recalls:
        simulated = dict(simulated)
        simulated["recalls"] = repetition.filter_repeated_recalls(simulated["recalls"])
    simulations[model_name] = simulated
print(
    "simulation_paths =",
    {model_name: str(path) for model_name, path in simulation_paths.items()},
)

Saved responses: results/simulations/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_broad_demo_best_of_3.h5
simulation_paths = {'CMR': 'results/simulations/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo_best_of_3.h5', 'eCMR_source_only': 'results/simulations/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_source_only_demo_best_of_3.h5', 'eCMR_broad': 'results/simulations/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_broad_demo_best_of_3.h5'}

12.4 Inspect the configured summaries

14 — Prepare configured model and observation comparisons 
comparison_groups = []
if (
    redo_figures
    and comparison_analysis_configs
    and any(not np.array_equal(mask, comparison_mask) for mask in selections.values())
):
    raise ValueError(
        "Shared comparison figures need matching selections; use separate jobs or disable comparison_analysis_configs."
    )

if redo_figures and simulations:
    observed = dict(data)
    if filter_repeated_recalls:
        observed["recalls"] = repetition.filter_repeated_recalls(observed["recalls"])
    datasets = [observed, *simulations.values()]
    names = ["Observed", *[display_labels[name] for name in simulations]]
    comparison_groups.append(
        {
            "analyses": comparison_analysis_configs,
            "datasets": datasets,
            "labels": names,
            "suffix": "",
        }
    )
    for dataset_index, (dataset, label) in enumerate(zip(datasets, names)):
        comparison_groups.append(
            {
                "analyses": single_analysis_configs,
                "datasets": [dataset],
                "labels": [label],
                "suffix": f"_single_{dataset_index}",
            }
        )
15 — Plot and save the configured benchmarks 
for group in comparison_groups:
    analysis_configs = group["analyses"]
    panel_data = group["datasets"]
    curve_labels = group["labels"]
    figure_suffix = group["suffix"]
    for analysis_index, analysis_config in enumerate(analysis_configs):
        plotter = import_from_string(analysis_config["target"])
        masks = [
            generate_trial_mask(
                dataset, analysis_config.get("trial_query", analysis_trial_query)
            )
            for dataset in panel_data
        ]
        masks = [
            trial_mask & comparison_mask if dataset is observed else trial_mask
            for dataset, trial_mask in zip(panel_data, masks)
        ]
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=analysis_config.get("figsize", figure_size))
        plot_options = {
            "labels": analysis_config.get("labels", curve_labels),
            "contrast_name": analysis_config.get("contrast_name", "Responses"),
            "confidence_level": confidence_level,
            "axis": ax,
            **analysis_config.get("kwargs", {}),
        }
        if analysis_config.get("color_cycle") is not None:
            plot_options["color_cycle"] = analysis_config["color_cycle"]
        plotter(panel_data, masks, **plot_options)
        ax.set_title(analysis_config.get("title", plotter.__name__))
        if analysis_config.get("ylim") is not None:
            ax.set_ylim(analysis_config["ylim"])
        suffix = (
            analysis_config.get("figure_suffix", plotter.__name__.removeprefix("plot_"))
            + figure_suffix
        )
        if (
            sum(
                other["target"] == analysis_config["target"]
                for other in analysis_configs
            )
            > 1
            and "figure_suffix" not in analysis_config
        ):
            suffix += f"_{analysis_index + 1}"
        save_figure(str(figure_dir), figure_str, suffix=suffix)

12.5 Continue with analysis

Pass the printed response paths to the behavioral analysis templates. Those procedures read saved responses and can compare them with observations or other simulations. Model comparison uses both the fit records and these responses. Custom datasets and model specifications enter through your saved fit records and parameters; the notebook body is shared.
